name: Eagle Springs
notes: TREAT OR BOIL, which is a stronger statement than the non-potable flag and a more useful one. EBRPD's map prints 'Water needs to be treated or boiled' beside the camp and the park page says 'All water should be treated or boiled before drinking'. So the water is present and usable with a stove and time, rather than simply undrinkable -- a distinction the potable column cannot make, and the reason that column is now three-valued rather than two. The District's corridor update lists this spigot as running while restating that all of it is non-potable; the two agree.

notes: Provided for horses. EBRPD states it is non-potable and must be filtered or treated for human consumption. No availability check has been logged, and a trough 3.2 miles in is the kind of source that goes dry without announcement.

name: Round Valley Backpack Camp
notes: Not working as of 2026-09-15, until further notice. NON-POTABLE CONFIRMED: the park page states the site's water is non-potable and must be boiled, treated or filtered -- so the conservative False recorded earlier on no evidence is now a sourced fact. The booking system's flat 'NO WATER' describes the outage rather than contradicting the park page. Drinking water is available at the Marsh Creek staging area, 3.4 to 3.6 miles before the site.

name: Dairy Glen Group Camp
notes: THE FIRST POTABLE SOURCE IN THIS PROJECT. Every other water source here is a spigot or trough EBRPD states is non-potable; this is described as a drinking fountain at a renovated, ADA-compliant group camp, so potable is the reading rather than an assumption -- but no page says the word 'potable', and no availability check has been logged.

name: Arroyo Flats Group Camp
notes: A drinking fountain at a PRIMITIVE group site, which is the difference from Dairy Glen's: that one sits at a renovated ADA-compliant camp, this one at a site EBRPD's own listing calls primitive with chemical toilets and no flush toilets or showers. Potable is still the reading -- a drinking fountain is for drinking -- but no page says the word, and no availability check has been logged. The second potable source in this project and the second never verified.

name: Corral Group Camp faucets
notes: TWO FAUCETS WITH SPIGOTS, AND THE AGENCY ITSELF SAYS THEY MAY NOT RUN. 'There are 2 water faucets with spigots, however, water sources at Las Trampas are unreliable and may run out of water at any time. Contact Park Staff ahead of your reservation for an update.' The park page and the park map carry the same warning in stronger words: 'The park's water supply is inconsistent and water may be unavailable at any time. Carry plenty of drinking water for yourself, your dog(s), and your horse(s).' EBRPD's own camping text says flatly that campers need to provide their own water. THE FIRST SOURCE HERE THE OPERATOR DESCRIBES AS UNRELIABLE RATHER THAN MERELY UNCHECKED, and that is a different fact. Every other row in this table is a source nobody has verified lately; this is one the agency verifies as unpromised. A dated check would not fix it -- running yesterday says nothing about tomorrow, which is what 'may run out at any time' means. POTABLE IS LEFT BLANK, not False. Nothing read says whether the water is drinkable when it flows; it is described as the park's drinking water supply and marked 'Drinking Water' in the map legend, which points at potable, and EBRPD never uses the word. Two faucets are recorded as ONE ROW because nothing distinguishes them -- no location, no separate status -- and inventing two rows would imply the project knows which is which.
